standard.title: Discuss perspectives
standard.description: discuss perspectives related to objects, people, places and events
standard.prior_knowledge: From Foundation (AC9HSFS03): Students shared a perspective on information, recognised that perspectives differ, and explained reasons for their own views.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students discuss perspectives related to objects, people, places and events, comparing their own views with those of others.

nodes.label: Comparing perspectives across time
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare their own daily lives with those of their parents, grandparents or familiar elders, and identify aspects of the past they would or would not want to experience.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare their own daily life with one aspect of a grandparent's or elder's daily life and state whether they would have preferred to live then or now, with a reason.
nodes.typical_width: Compare daily lives with parents, grandparents, elders or familiar older people; identify which aspects of the past they would or would not want to experience; explain reasons for preferences.
wider: Interview a family member or elder about what they valued most about their childhood and compare perspectives across generations
Explore how perspectives on the same aspect of daily life (e.g. schooling, play, food) differ between generations

response_modes.reason: Real intergenerational comparison — through interview or family discussion — provides far richer perspective material than textbook examples.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Intergenerational perspective-sharing connects students' historical learning directly to family relationships, making historical empathy concrete and personally meaningful.
success_criteria: Compares their own life with at least one aspect of a parent's or grandparent's life
States a preference and gives at least one reason for it

nodes.label: Personal preferences about places and events
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share personal preferences about their world (favourite weather, activities, places, celebrations) and explain why they are favoured.
nodes.minimum_width: Share a preference about at least one aspect of their world (weather, place, celebration) and explain at least one reason for that preference.
nodes.typical_width: Share personal preferences about weather, activities, places, celebrations and objects from the past; explain reasons for preferences; listen to and respect differing preferences from peers.
wider: Compare preferences across the class and look for patterns — do preferences relate to cultural background, family experience or personal interests?
Discuss whether personal preferences should influence decisions about places (e.g. what should be in a park) and why

response_modes.reason: Explaining preferences about places and events is the culminating perspective task — it integrates personal experience with HASS content knowledge.

success_criteria: Shares a preference about at least one topic with a reason
Listens to and acknowledges a different preference from a peer
